insights.title: More very hot days
insights.body: Days at 35 °C or hotter went from about 4 to 22 a year. Heat at flowering cuts yields of rice, maize and most pulses.

insights.title: Rain is more than crops can use
insights.body: Rain exceeds crop water demand by about 3148 mm a year. Waterlogging and runoff are bigger risks than drought.

insights.title: Best-matched crops for this area

outlook.method: Theil-Sen trend + Mann-Kendall test on 2001-2024 yearly data, extended to 2035 with an 80% prediction range. Where there is no clear trend, the 2001-2024 average is projected. Statistical extrapolation, not a climate-model forecast.

consequences.headline: About 10 more scorching days a year by 2035
consequences.detail: Days at 35 °C or hotter are heading from about 11 to 21 a year. Heat during flowering kills pollen, so grain and pod set drop — Soybean, Groundnut, Black gram and Rice are most exposed.
consequences.action: Sow so flowering misses the hottest weeks, or pick heat-tolerant varieties.

consequences.headline: +0.8 °C warmer on average by 2035
consequences.detail: The yearly average moves from 26.0 °C to about 26.8 °C. Most recommended crops stay inside their temperature range.
consequences.action: Watch heat stress in cool-climate crops; earlier sowing helps.
